title: Quantifying Xenografted Human Cancer Cells in Zebrafish Larvae Using Cellpose
author: Köpke, Lembke, et al.

steps.title: Remove larvae from agarose
steps.instruction: Using sharp Dumont forceps or similar utensils, scrape an outline around each larva starting at the yolk height, peel off all agarose without touching the larva, and release the larva.

steps.title: Transfer larvae to fresh E3
steps.instruction: Aspirate each larva with a 1.5 mL pipette and place it into a petri dish containing fresh E3 medium supplemented with methylene blue.

steps.title: Select successfully transplanted larvae
steps.instruction: Under a fluorescent microscope, identify larvae that display the red CMTPX‑labeled GSCs in the midbrain and retain only those individuals.

steps.title: Incubate larvae at 34 °C
steps.instruction: Place the selected larvae in an incubator set to 34 °C for 2–3 days (or the desired duration), maintaining this temperature to support both zebrafish and human cell viability.

steps.title: Daily health screening
steps.instruction: Each day, examine larvae for normal morphology; discard any dead, malformed, or unhealthy individuals and return the remainder to the 34 °C incubator.

steps.title: Discard unsuitable larvae before staining
steps.instruction: Remove larvae that are dead, have tail curvature, heart‑sack edema, head/eye swelling, or lack visible fluorescent GSCs or have cells outside the midbrain.

steps.title: Anesthetize and fix larvae
steps.instruction: Transfer each larva to a 1.5–2 mL Eppendorf tube, remove residual E3, add 1× Tricaine in 1× E3 to anesthetize, then fix in 4 % paraformaldehyde for at least 24 h at 4 °C (or 3 h at 20 °C).

steps.title: Store fixed larvae (optional pause)
steps.instruction: After fixation, keep larvae in 1× PBS at 4 °C in the dark for up to 7 days (do not exceed to preserve quality).

steps.title: Remove paraformaldehyde and PBS washes
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, discard the paraformaldehyde waste, then wash the fixed larvae three times with 1× PBS for 5 min each.

steps.title: Wash with PBS‑Triton
steps.instruction: Wash the larvae three times with 0.3 % PBS‑Triton X‑100 (PBS‑T) for 5 min each.

steps.title: Permeabilize larvae
steps.instruction: Incubate larvae in 10 µg/mL Proteinase K in PBS at 37 °C for 45 min (adjust to 15 min for 24–48 hpf or 30 min for 48–96 hpf larvae).

steps.title: Post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Fix the permeabilized larvae in 4 % paraformaldehyde for 20 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Wash after post‑fix
steps.instruction: Wash larvae three times with PBS‑T for 5 min each.

steps.title: Block with BSA
steps.instruction: Prepare 3 % bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS‑T (dilute 20 % BSA stock) and incubate larvae for 1 h at 20 °C.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: In 100 µL total volume of 3 % BSA/PBS‑T, add mouse recombinant anti‑human nucleoli antibody at 1:100 dilution; incubate larvae in Eppendorf tubes on a rocking platform for 12–18 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash primary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash larvae at least five times with PBS‑T, each wash lasting 5 min.

steps.title: Second block
steps.instruction: Incubate larvae again in 3 % BSA/PBS‑T for 1 h at 20 °C.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: In 100 µL of 3 % BSA/PBS‑T, add goat‑anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 at 1:500 dilution; incubate on a rocking platform for 12–18 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Wash larvae at least five times with PBS‑T, each wash 5 min (performed the following day).

steps.title: DAPI staining
steps.instruction: Incubate larvae in 1:1000 DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS at 4 °C in the dark for 5–7 days.

steps.title: Final PBS wash
steps.instruction: After DAPI incubation, wash the larvae once with PBS.

steps.title: Store stained larvae
steps.instruction: Keep stained larvae in 1× PBS at 4 °C in the dark for up to 14 days before microscopy (avoid longer storage to maintain image quality).

description: The protocol describes the injection of human glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) into the midbrain of live zebrafish larvae, followed by the quantification of GSCs. This protocol can be adapted and applied to inject various human cancer cell lines and patient-derived xenografts into different locations within zebrafish larvae. To locate the cells, staining with CellTracker dye (for example, CMTPX) or the expression of a fluorescent protein is required. Furthermore, for quantification, a human cell-specific antibody is required. Here, we describe the injection of a patient-derived GSC line stained with CMTPX red and anti-human nucleoli antibody. Cancer (stem) cells can be commercially purchased (e.g., atcc.org), obtained from colleagues or isolated directly from patients as described previously.1
